answer: Slashing Reputation Escrow defends against Sybil attacks. First, agents must lock collateral in an onyx vault. Second, peer observers use a prism of behavioral metrics to validate truth. Third, any detected fraud triggers immediate asset seizure. To launch a fake swarm, an attacker faces a cost of $500,000 in bonds and 45 days of scrutiny. This ensures no cheap relic of a fake identity can bypass the gate. It is like trying to enter a high-security vault where every single new guest must pay a massive, non-refundable entry fee that exceeds their total net worth.
